data.turoyo: Səmlan ṣluṯo, mqarawle lu faṭəryarxo. Mšəḥle i ʕito w mqadšole, <...>
data.translation: We held a prayer service; the patriarch celebrated the liturgy. He anointed the church and consecrated it. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit/1 cell, explicit church object and separate consecration predicate; expands beyond human patients.

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Eeeee, šamoše, kuhne w fəlan. Kul d kowe faṣəl gədəzzox, məšḥatle bu zayto mqadšo, bi merən, bu zayto mqadšo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: Yeeeees, deacons, priests and so on. Whenever there is a section, you go and anoint him with the holy oil, with chrism, with the holy oil.

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 cell; second-person subject, patient suffix and named oil/chrism instrument. Patient identity is not recoverable from this verse.

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Yaʕqub u šliḥo mən komər, komər: "I naqqa d kiyawlox, qray lak kuhne di ʕito d məšḥilox bu zayto d mṣalallox, ḥaylo di ṣluṯo, rabo yo!
data.translation: Father Brahim: What does James the apostle say? He says, “When you become ill, call the priests of the church to anoint you with oil and pray for you; the power of prayer is great!”

rationale: Thin Infectum/1 cell; plural priests, second-person patient and oil instrument in an explicit sickness-and-summons frame.

summary: Both supplied occurrences are already represented. No new stem, form, sense or example is needed.

The Preterit mšiḥoli indexes a first-person agent and feminine object; the Infectum koməšhi takes the people as object. Anointing the deceased versus the sick changes patient/context, not the inherited salben meaning.
The German addition about a cross on forehead and right hand has no separate action verb in the supplied 94/53 Turoyo. It is not mined as an independently attested collocation.
No new Idiomatic phrases or participant-specific sense split.
Jan explicitly supplies b-marked oil and chrism instruments and personal patient suffixes. Such ritual content remains salben rather than a light-verb expression or new numbered sense.
Jan 2.31/4874 quotes a scriptural instruction in Turoyo; its transparent məšḥilox form contrasts with genuinely Syriac inflectional quotations encountered elsewhere.
faṣəl in Jan 2.31/4870 is not explained by the machine word “section”; preserve the source and keep ordination versus sick-person context unresolved.
94/53: h in koməšhi versus ḥ in the existing glossary transcription requires collation; no silent normalization.
Confirm the LB 9 to Talay 1/9 reference correspondence if the editors standardize references; the existing citation has not been replaced.
What does faṣəl denote at Jan 2.31/4870, and who is -le? Does this concern ordination rather than sick-person anointing?
Does church anointing at Jan 2.10/2705 involve chrism on the building/altar specifically? The source names only i ʕito.
A church building is anointed alongside its consecration; this extends the patient class of salben. mqadšole separately expresses consecration, so no new “consecrate” sense is inferred for mšḥ.
